iterations.label: iteration 1
iterations.rationale: Moved nearly all flexible load out of the night and into the 09:00-16:00 midday surplus window. Prices there are lowest, and the -$10/MWh window credit makes hours 9-12 net-negative. The cheapest hours 9-11 are packed close to the 300 MW cap. Remaining 3h and 2h jobs plus all code reviews spill into hours 12-15. Only IN13 (deadline 9) runs early, at hour 5, and the evening peak is avoided entirely.

iterations.label: iteration 2
iterations.rationale: Kept the iteration-1 structure, which fills the cheapest window hours 9-12. Hours 9-12 are now packed closer to the 300 MW cap (about 296-300 MW each); before, hour 12 was at 289 MW. I did this by reshuffling the inbox digests and moving CO12 and CO04 into hour 12. DE04, DE09 and most code reviews moved from hour 13 to hours 14-15, which are slightly cheaper, and nothing runs during the evening peak.

iterations.label: iteration 3
iterations.rationale: Kept everything inside the cheap 09:00-16:00 surplus window and repacked the jobs to fill the cheapest hours, 09-12, closer to the 300 MW cap. Each of those hours now carries about 295-298 MW. To do this, all 4-hour jobs start at 09, five large 3-hour jobs run 09-11, and the remaining 3-hour and 2-hour deep jobs start at 12. The early-deadline inbox digests fill the leftover room in 09-12. Most code reviews and the later-deadline digests moved from hour 13 to hours 14-15, which are slightly cheaper, so hour 16 stays empty and nothing runs in the evening peak or above the cap.

iterations.label: iteration 4
iterations.rationale: Valid plan rebuilt from the best schedule (iteration 2), with every job given a start hour. The cheapest window hours (10, 11, 9, 12) are packed close to the 300 MW cap. All 4h jobs and OV04 start at 9, the large 3h jobs sit in 9-12, and overflow 3h/2h jobs plus most code reviews go to the near-zero-cost hours 13-15. IN13 stays at hour 5 because its deadline forces an early run, and nothing runs in the evening peak.

iterations.label: iteration 5
iterations.rationale: Kept the iteration-4 packing, which already fills hours 9-12 to roughly 290-299 MW with no cap overflow. Moved IN04 from 12:00 to 09:00, using hour 9's 10.85 MW of slack at a lower effective price. That freed room at 12:00, so CO09 moves from 14:00 into it, shifting a little more energy into the cheapest in-window hours. Expected gain is small, about $30 versus iteration 4, which may only roughly match the best score so far. All hourly loads stay at or below 300 MW and all deadlines are met.

iterations.label: iteration 6
iterations.rationale: Kept hours 9-12 packed near the 300 MW cap (about 298/297/297/296 MW), since those are the cheapest hours after the $10/MWh window credit. Moved load out of hour 13, which is slightly pricier than 14-15, into 14-15. To do that, every 3-4 h job now fits entirely inside 9-12 where possible, and most 2 h code-review and deep-reasoning jobs sit at 14-15. IN13 stays at 05:00, its cheapest feasible hour, and all deadlines and the cap are respected.

iterations.label: iteration 7
iterations.rationale: Kept the iteration-6 schedule, which was the best so far with no violations and no peak-hour energy. One small change: OV06 now starts at 12 (running 12-14) instead of 13, so it uses the cheaper midday hour 12 in place of hour 15. To keep hour 12 at about 299.5 MW, under the 300 MW cap, the inbox jobs IN15 and IN11 move from 12 to 14, which is still within their deadlines; by my calculation this nets roughly $7 of savings.

iterations.label: iteration 8
iterations.rationale: Iteration 7 is close to optimal. All flexible load sits in the 09:00-16:00 surplus window. The cheapest hours (09-12) are filled to the 300 MW cap, and the remainder goes to 13-15, where the net cost is near zero. Every single-job move I tested (for example, CO01 to 14 with IN11 to 12) came out cost-neutral or worse, so I am keeping the best plan unchanged to lock in -4,277 with no cap or deadline violations.
